question.problem:
Which of the following vector-valued functions are continuous on $[-1,1]?$

  

$$
\begin{aligned}p(s) & =|{s}^{2}-1|\,i+\frac{s+1}{s}\,j+2{s}^{2}\,k \\ q(s) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(s-1)\,i+({s}^{2}+1)\,j+\operatorname{cos}⁡s\,k \\ r(s) & =\operatorname{sin}⁡s\,i-2\operatorname{tan}⁡s\,j+\operatorname{csc}⁡s\,k\end{aligned}
$$

choices.value: None of the functions are continuous on $[-1,1]$

current_example.problem: Is the vector function $\mathbf f(t) = -\sin t \,\mathbf i + (t^2 + 1)\,\mathbf j + \tan t\,\mathbf k$ continuous at $t = 0?$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's compute the limit of $\mathbf f (t)$ as $t$ approaches $0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) & =⟨{lim}_{t\to 0}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}({t}^{2}+1),\,{lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{tan}⁡t⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡0,\,{0}^{2}+1,\,\operatorname{tan}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =f(0)\end{aligned}
$$

So $\displaystyle \lim_{t \rightarrow t_0} \mathbf f (t) = \mathbf f (t_0)$ and therefore $\mathbf f (t)$ is continuous at $t=0.$
